commit_message:
Reuse c->argv after command execution to reduce memory allocation overhead (#13521)

inspred by https://github.com/redis/redis/pull/12730

Before this PR, we allocate new memory to store the user command
arguments, however, if the size of the current `c->argv` is larger than
the current command, we can reuse the previously allocated argv to avoid
allocating new memory for the current command.
And we will free `c->argv` in client cron when the client is idle for 2
seconds.

---------

Co-authored-by: Ozan Tezcan <ozantezcan@gmail.com>

fix_commit_message:
Fix crash due to cron argv release (#13725)

Introduced by https://github.com/redis/redis/issues/13521

If the client argv was released due to a timeout before sending the
complete command, `argv_len` will be reset to 0.
When argv is parsed again and resized, requesting a length of 0 may
result in argv being NULL, then leading to a crash.

And fix a bug that `argv_len` is not updated correctly in
`replaceClientCommandVector()`.

---------

Co-authored-by: ShooterIT <wangyuancode@163.com>
Co-authored-by: meiravgri <109056284+meiravgri@users.noreply.github.com>
agent_reasoning: Merged diff composed mechanically by cherry-picking fix 08d714d0e5d5 on top of intro 701f06657d20 via git's 3-way merge. Vulnerability (NullPointerDereference): Redis's clientsCron periodically frees a client's command-argument vector (c->argv) if the client appears idle, to reduce per-connection memory overhead. The idle check introduced in PR #13521 only verified `!c->argv || c->argc`, which fails to detect a client that is idle in the middle of sending a multibulk command (header received, args not yet complete), a state identifiable via a non-zero c->multibulklen with c->argc still 0. In that state the cron job frees argv and resets argv_len to 0 concurrently with the client's own parsing state machine. When the client subsequently sends more data and the parser (processMultibulkBuffer) resumes, the growth calculation for argv uses the now-zeroed argv_len, which can cause a zero-size realloc and leave c->argv as NULL while argc/multibulklen still indicate pending arguments, leading to a NULL pointer dereference / crash when the parser writes the next argument into argv[c->argc]. Root cause: Missing/incorrect idle-check condition: the function used to decide whether it's safe to free a client's argv only considered c->argc, not c->multibulklen, so it incorrectly treated a client that is mid-command-parse (multibulk header received but args pending) as idle/safe-to-free. This is compounded by replaceClientCommandVector() not keeping c->argv_len in sync with c->argc, which the companion fix also addresses.
